motivation: Community-insurance v1 showed that source points with at least one alternative seagrass were more likely to remain seagrass-occupied after exact-point Thalassia loss. Test whether that binary effect extends to a diversity gradient: more pre-loss alternative seagrass taxa predict greater habitat-state retention.

source.stable_point_id: Point-event locationID constructed upstream as Transect + Site/meter-mark identity
source.seagrass_definition: Present occurrence rows in order Alismatales
source.point_year_consistency: Retain only point-years for which repeated visits agree on the complete present-Alismatales scientificName set.

eligible_transition: same stable point observed in consecutive years; source-year Thalassia present; target-year Thalassia absent

predictor.name: source_alternative_seagrass_richness
predictor.definition: count of distinct source-year present Alismatales scientificName values excluding Thalassia testudinum
predictor.treatment: integer count, entered linearly in the primary logistic model; no post-outcome binning

endpoint: target-year any seagrass present at the same point

model.scaling: StandardScaler fitted to numeric predictors within each bootstrap fit
model.bootstrap: stable-transect node-cluster bootstrap; all point-loss transitions from a sampled node travel together

hypothesis.statement: Greater pre-loss alternative seagrass richness predicts a higher probability that an exact meter mark remains occupied by seagrass after Thalassia loss.
hypothesis.estimand: log-odds coefficient for source_alternative_seagrass_richness, adjusted for loss year and water body
hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-cluster bootstrap interval for richness coefficient > 0

descriptive_outputs: target occupancy fraction by exact source richness value
transition and node counts by richness
predicted occupancy probability at observed richness values from the full fitted model
claim_boundary: Post-hoc ecological hypothesis motivated by the supported binary source-mixture insurance result.
A positive richness coefficient is consistent with biodiversity insurance but does not prove causal insurance, facilitation, or niche complementarity.
Persistent habitat quality could cause both higher source richness and target seagrass retention.
Richness counts observed taxa at the annual point visit and is subject to detection variability.
Do not change the linear richness treatment, transition/node minima, period, segment pool, or endpoint after response opening.
